decisions: One schema for a composition and for a single text request: a single request is a one-layer composition, so there is no second input format to keep in step with text layers.

No builder API: builder programs run in Node and cannot shape text. Measurements are layer-local and do not depend on a layer's position, so a program places itself from its own saved measurement (`--output`, then readMeasure/measured in research/editorial-titles-et7a/layout.ts, which refuses a measurement made for other copy or size).

`--output` writes the report only once measured, replacing the file in one step: a shell `>` redirect empties the file the program reads before measuring finishes (found when the two-pass flow failed with "Unexpected end of JSON input").

The browser page setup (Vite middleware server, pinned Chromium, cleanup on abort) moved from composition-lint.ts into composition-browser-page.ts unchanged and is shared; lint keeps its composition-lint-vite- cache prefix, measure uses composition-measure-vite-.
Measure prepares no video, sequence, image or audio media (text layout does not depend on them) and refuses compositions with native 3D (comp-measure-unsupported).

samePath: Node: readCompositionDocument, validatePreparedAssets (fonts), checkCompositionFonts (ET1 coverage), as comp validate. Browser: loadCompositionFonts and prepareCompositionText, exactly as rendering calls them, with a bounds-only canvas source (the one text frame discovery already uses), then the shaped layouts of prepared typography. Ink boxes are the shaped clusters' measureText bounds; motionBounds is the same `bounds` the renderer passes as textBounds.

output.coordinates: layer-local pixels: origin at the layer's position, y down; `origin` gives the composition position when the layer is a plain translation (no anchor, scale, rotation, skew, parent, camera, camera2d the layer follows, driver, periodic motion, expression or constraint that moves it, or precomp)
output.perState: motionBounds (render textBounds), advance, ink, base-font metrics (size, ascent, descent, capHeight, xHeight, lineHeight, tracking)
output.perLine: advance box, ink, baseline, capTop, xTop
output.perSpan: the span's own font metrics; per line: text, advance, ink, capTop, xTop
output.perWord: word units as `word` animators move them (Unicode word segmentation; punctuation joins the word before it): text, line, spans, advance, ink
output.outline: largest drawn strokeWidth over reachable visible frames (0.25 px grid), extent = strokeWidth / 2, outlined ink per layer and line
output.decorations: kind, thickness, offset, painted box per line at full reveal, and for highlight/strike centredOffset {cap, ink}; brush and ink line styles flagged approximate
output.notMeasured: text without a pinned font (listed with the reason); layer effects other than drop shadow and glow; native 3D compositions
output.effects: per enabled light.drop-shadow and light.glow: sigma (shadow blur, glow radius), offset on the renderer's 1/16 px grid (keyed extremes), strength, conservative paint box (renderer bounds rule: shadow ⌈3σ⌉+1, glow 3σ+2), visible box at 5% coverage (σ·Q⁻¹(0.05/strength) past a straight edge of the source); source = ink ∪ outline ∪ decoration paint; state-level paint and visible include them

pixelAgreement.rule: A rendered edge is the first or last pixel row or column with at least 12% coverage of the element's rendered colour over its background (on the blend line between the two, within 24 levels), as a half-open box; measured boxes are placed by their layer origins.
pixelAgreement.result: 49 of 57 edges within 1 px; worst 1.82 px (LEATHER ink top)
pixelAgreement.why2px: An exact edge reads up to 1 px outside under the half-open, 12% rule; Chrome's antialiasing and its glyph bounds add the rest. Fractional layer origins spread edges further (worst 1.82 px before origins were rounded, with tops about 1 px high), so layout.ts centreOn/topAt return whole pixels.

limitations: The outline width is the largest any visible glyph reaches over the reachable frames; an outline animated between widths reports its widest.
Decorations with brush or ink line styles report their nominal band (approximate: true).
Highlight thickness defaults use the layer's base font cap height, as drawing does, even over a span in another font.

Effect sizes are in layer pixels, which are the effect's pixels only when the layer is unscaled (see `origin`).

effects.samePath: Drop shadow: the renderer's Gaussian kernel (shadowGaussianKernel, σ = blur, radius ⌈3σ⌉) and offset quantisation to 1/16 px (shadow-effects.ts), and the bounds rule of its definition (expandBounds: ⌈3σ⌉+1). Glow: pixel-effects.ts glow (alpha × thresholded luminance, CSS blur(radius), screen at intensity) and evaluate/effects.ts's margin 3·radius+2. Effects apply to the layer's whole drawing, so they grow from ink ∪ outline ∪ decorations ∪ container.
effects.coverageThreshold: 5% (about 13/255). A Gaussian tail has no hard edge; `visible` is where a long straight edge's effect falls to 5%. Thin strokes and corners carry less mass, so their visible edge lies inside (treat visibleReach as the upper end for thin scripts).

colourShift.question: #2F6F6A (47,111,106) read as (31,97,92) in the ET6a test's PNG frames: which stage changes colour?
colourShift.minimalCase: 200×200 composition, paper #F4EFE2, a solid #2F6F6A box and Bebas text in #2F6F6A; then a 64×64 BT.709 limited-range lossless H.264 clip of RGB (47,111,106) as a video layer. Inputs and outputs local only (benchmarks/results/colour/).

stages.rendererCanvas: Exact. Read straight from the preview canvas in the pinned browser: box and text (47,111,106), paper (244,239,226). Shapes and text shift the same way at every later stage.
stages.explicitProfiles: Deliberate and documented (composition reference, Output formats: 'Explicit profiles convert encoded-sRGB renderer bytes to BT.709 RGB'). createCompositionOutputConversion maps each sRGB byte to linear and then the BT.709 OETF: 47→31, 111→97, 244→243. png8 is tagged cICP 1/1/0/1 (BT.709 transfer, full range); h264 is tagged BT.709 transfer/matrix, tv range, and decodes to (28,95,89).
stages.defaultMp4: `comp render` without --format applies no transfer conversion: the box decodes to (44,109,103), i.e. sRGB code values with only YUV 4:2:0 rounding, but it carries the same BT.709 primaries/transfer/matrix tags as --format h264.
stages.videoInput: compositionMediaColorFilter decodes BT.709-transfer sources through the inverse OETF into sRGB: a clip decoding to (44,109,103) sits in the canvas as (62,124,119). --format png8 re-encodes it to (46,111,106), a round trip; the default MP4 writes (60,122,117), up to 16 levels lighter than the source.
stages.frameExtraction: ffmpeg rawvideo rgb24 returns stored code values and ignores the PNG's cICP transfer, so the ET6a test compared measurements with BT.709-OETF code values instead of the renderer's sRGB.

colourShift.cause: Not a renderer defect and not an encoder range/matrix error: the shift is the explicit profiles' documented sRGB→BT.709 OETF re-encoding, read without colour management. It exposes a real inconsistency: the default MP4 and --format h264 carry identical BT.709 tags but different code values for the same composition, and the default MP4 lifts BT.709 footage (input inverse OETF without output OETF).
colourShift.decision: Was an owner decision, because each direction visibly changes outputs: (a) give the default MP4 the explicit profiles' OETF encode (footage round-trips; every authored colour in default MP4s darkens in the shadows, unlike the ET7a renders the owner accepted), or (b) treat BT.709 SDR as display-equivalent to sRGB in and out (no transfer conversion; matches how players show BT.709 and the default MP4's graphics; changes explicit-profile outputs and footage values in the canvas, so pixel lint and legibility numbers over footage). Either is a versioned output change with affected baselines listed. Recommended: (b), because players display BT.709 with a display EOTF rather than the inverse camera OETF, and the canvas then holds footage as viewers see it, which ET3/ET6b contrast depends on. Not implemented. Decided 2026-11-16, owner: "Match players" (option b): treat BT.709-tagged video as equivalent to sRGB, with no transfer conversion in or out. Implemented separately on codex/composition-colour-accuracy (from main), with its own results file docs/composition-colour-accuracy-results.json.
colourShift.et6aEvidence: Corrected: the test now reads frames straight from the renderer canvas (tests/helpers/renderer-frame.ts) and asserts each authored colour is drawn exactly. Results are unchanged: 49 of 57 edges within 1 px, worst 1.82 px (the transfer is per pixel and moved no edge beyond rounding).

decided.choice: Treat BT.709-tagged video as equivalent to sRGB; no transfer conversion on the way in or out.
